findings.message: Target 'temper.cli@swift-universal.clia.sh' uses user-facing strings but has no approved i18n copy-package receipt.
User-facing string literal must come from an approved generated i18n copy package.

heuristics.description: User-facing copy crosses the target boundary without an approved generated-package passport.
heuristics.name: Missing Passport

heuristics.description: User-facing prose has escaped the typed catalog and is authored loose in product source.
heuristics.name: Loose Copy

heuristics.description: Product code takes a localization side door around the approved generated accessor boundary.
heuristics.name: Side Door

heuristics.description: An approved import dresses the target as adopted while none of its generated accessors are used.
heuristics.name: Costume Import

heuristics.description: Development-only vapor has leaked across the release boundary.
heuristics.name: Vapor Leak

heuristics.description: A generated accessor appears without a reproducible dependency on its owning module.
heuristics.name: Ghost Dependency

heuristics.description: An approved declaration has no live generated-accessor sink in the scanned target.
heuristics.name: Orphaned Declaration

heuristics.description: A copy-shaped module presents no approved publication receipt proving its identity.
heuristics.name: Counterfeit Package

heuristics.description: The generated accessor index cannot account for every declared canonical key exactly once.
heuristics.name: Broken Index

heuristics.description: Multiple imported packages contest ownership of the same canonical key.
heuristics.name: Key Turf War

heuristics.description: A live generated accessor resolves to a key missing from imported publication declarations.
heuristics.name: Undocumented Use

heuristics.description: One imported module answers to multiple approved receipts, splitting publication authority.
heuristics.name: Split Authority

heuristics.description: Multiple generated accessor aliases lead to the same canonical key.
heuristics.name: Alias Maze

heuristics.description: One publication receipt counts the same canonical key more than once.
heuristics.name: Double Entry

heuristics.description: A declared locale shard looks complete but cannot materialize every canonical catalog record into target resources.
heuristics.name: Translation Mirage

heuristics.description: A translation changes, drops, duplicates, or retags formatting placeholders at the locale boundary.
heuristics.name: Placeholder Smuggling

heuristics.description: A locale silently resolves through source-language fallback instead of proving a localized artifact.
heuristics.name: Fallback Fog

heuristics.description: A published locale exists in inventory but no declared product route can reach it.
heuristics.name: Dead Tongue

heuristics.description: A canonical key and its generated accessor diverge from the product's declared key-shape grammar.
heuristics.name: Key Shape Drift

heuristics.description: Distinct meanings are forced through one key without typed context evidence proving that the reuse is intentional.
heuristics.name: Context Collapse
